title: Console Strata: MVP slice & scope-reduction decision log for Dashboards / Tracing / Cost Breakdown
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: our full Console telemetry surface (dozens of cards, high-cardinality trace views, and per-route cost breakdown) is taking too long to build and will jeopardize the April release. The Platform team and Infra flagged backend readiness constraints (indexing bandwidth and query cost), and Design requested a narrower initial set so we can ship a coherent experience. This ticket documents the final scope reductions, rationale, explicit acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for an MVP that delivers value to customers while keeping engineering effort bounded.
decisions: Ship an MVP that focuses on 'Strata' — one prioritized card per domain (Performance, Reliability, Cost) plus a lightweight trace sampler view. This reduces initial backend load and UI polish scope.
Drop high-cardinality breakdowns (per-model, per-client) from MVP; expose them later behind a feature flag in Dedicated/Private only.
Surface synthetic or sampled traces for the tracing view in the MVP (no full-span flamegraphs or deep span search).
Limit cost breakdown to aggregated route-level deltas and 7-day rolling token trends; detailed per-route per-model slices deferred.
Implement graceful degraded mode: if telemetry backends are unavailable show cached 24h snapshot and clear messaging with CTA to retry or view reduced set.
Canary rollout to 10% of orgs with opt-in flag; open beta after stability criteria met.
Telemetry privacy: ensure no PII is rendered in traces for MVP; mask any request metadata that might contain user content.
tradeoffs: Pro: Faster release and lower query cost. Con: Some customers (platform teams) lose early access to fine-grained cost attribution.
Pro: Smaller UI surface reduces QA burden. Con: First impressions may underwhelm power users used to deep diagnostics.
Accept increased manual support for feature-flagged rollouts to handle edge cases until full automation is ready.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Dashboards — Deliver 3 core insight cards: median route latency (P50), 95th percentile latency (P95), and token throughput (tokens/min) for the last 7 days. Each card must load with meaningful data within 1.2s (median) for orgs with <5k RPS equivalents.

AC-2: Tracing — Provide a sampled-trace viewer showing span timeline for up to 10 traces per route, with ability to filter by error vs success, and at least one example of a trace linked from a P95 spike event. No deep-span search required for MVP.

AC-3: Cost breakdown — Implement aggregated route-level cost delta card (7-day change vs prior 7 days) and a per-route token trend sparkline. Numbers must reconcile with billing exports within a 3% delta for the sampled test dataset.

AC-4: Graceful degradation — If telemetry backend returns 5xx or times out, Console must present a cached 24h snapshot and an explanatory banner with retry CTA; system must not crash or block other Console surfaces.

AC-5: Observability SLOs — New endpoints introduced for dashboard data must have 99th percentile response time <2s and error rate <0.5% in canary traffic over a 48h window to proceed to wider rollout.
AC-6: UX acceptance — Design review signoff on the three cards and trace viewer interactions (comments from Design resolved or documented).
AC-7: Security/Privacy — No raw request content or user identifiers appear in the trace viewer; automated sanitizer test must pass in CI.
AC-8: Rollout gating — Metrics, incident checklist, and rollback playbook documented and linked; canary promotion to 50% requires zero P1 incidents and stable SLOs for 72h.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: create focused PRD subset and endpoint contracts for the three cards and sampled tracing (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-02-26).
2) Infra: run a query-cost simulation against sampled dataset to validate backend QPS for 3-card cadence (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-01).
3) Design: deliver high-fidelity mocks for the compact cards and trace list (owner: Lian Chen, due: 2026-02-28).
4) Security: run automated sanitizer on instrumented traces and sign off (owner: Omar Khalid, due: 2026-03-05).
5) PM: prepare canary rollout checklist and customer communication templates (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-10).
